articles.title: 15/18 A Place to Heal review – heartfelt docu-realist study of a French teen psychiatric facility
articles.summary: Venice film festival Director Cédric Kahn combines compassion with coolly detailed forensic scrutiny in this genre-challenging film which puts a troubled love triangle at the centre of the story.
body: Veteran French director Cédric Kahn brings us a movie in a classic French vein: a docu-realist study of an institution, in this case a state psychiatric facility for teenagers between 15 and 18; with scenes in treatment suites, recreation areas, dorms and interview rooms. It’s something to compare perhaps with Laurent Cantet’s The Class, or Nicolas Philibert’s On the Adamant, or Canadian film-maker Denis Côte’s That Kind of Summer.

Kahn’s film is powerful and committed, although sometimes the acting comes close to shouty improv youth theatre. The tone is of course one of compassion, combined with coolly detailed forensic scrutiny, though audiences might be intrigued at Kahn’s use of Purcell’s Funeral Sentences on the soundtrack, music notably used by Kubrick in A Clockwork Orange, a film in which delinquent youth are treated more roughly. Kahn himself plays one of the senior medical staff, part of the gallery of authority figures – doctors, nurses, orderlies, therapists and a nervous intern – who are almost as affected by the institutional drama as the troubled young people themselves.
points: Venice film festival Director Cédric Kahn combines compassion with coolly detailed forensic scrutiny in this genre-challenging film which puts a troubled love triangle at the centre of the story.

articles.title: ‘Like a tired boxer, battered by applause’: as Andrew Scott’s biopic premieres, Richard Eyre remembers Ian Charleson’s superb, near-death Hamlet
articles.summary: In 1989, the Chariots of Fire actor took on the incredible task of playing Shakespeare’s prince while terminally ill from Aids. This weekend sees the world premiere of Elsinore, a new film about the episode, itself heavily-tipped for awards.
body: Ian Charleson was one of the finest actors of his generation and an important figure in the fight for gay rights. Yet the extraordinary circumstances of his final performance as Hamlet, just months before his death, are less familiar.

Now, a new film is bringing that haunting production back to life. Elsinore, directed by Simon Stone and starring Andrew Scott as the Scottish actor, will premiere at Telluride this weekend before opening the London film festival in October.

Charleson was 40 and terminally ill with Aids when he was cast as Hamlet in Richard Eyre’s 1989 production at the National Theatre, after Daniel Day-Lewis abruptly left the role. Charleson had first played Hamlet 15 years earlier and persuaded Eyre to let him reprise it, despite the director’s misgivings about his health.
“Ian was very bright, very witty, mischievous,” Eyre told the Guardian. “He was beyond good-looking. He was beautiful, and he had a beautiful singing voice.”

articles.title: Maria Bartiromo vs. Fox News: The Anchor’s Pivot Between MAGA Politics and Wall Street Likely Spurred Fallout
articles.summary: Maria Bartiromo was brought to Fox to cover the ins and outs of Wall Street, and make the company a bigger presence in the world of business-news cable. But her growing interest in punditry and opinion left Fox increasingly uncovered before the law.
body: In June, Bartiromo read an apology on air after entrepreneur and “Shark Tank” personality Kevin O’Leary appeared on one of her shows a month earlier and made the false accusation that detractors of a data center he wanted to build in Utah were being funded by China. For executives at Fox News Media, it may have been the second-to-last straw.

Bartiromo is believed to have passed along a directive issued to executive producers at Fox Business Network to the White House, according to a person familiar with the matter, and those instructions may have cautioned Fox Business staffers against support to outlandish claims made by President Donald Trump in public remarks. Divulging confidential company information to an outside party would likely be seen as a violation of terms of employment.

But her growing interest in punditry and opinion left Fox increasingly uncovered before the law.

articles.title: Latcho Drom director Tony Gatlif dies aged 77
articles.summary: Film-maker acclaimed for his celebrations of Roma culture had been working on a ‘historical film project’ in Provence. Tony Gatlif, the French director of more than 20 films that mostly concentrated on celebrating Roma culture across the world, has died aged 77.
body: His family said in a statement to AFP that Gatlif died on Wednesday of “a health issue” while working on a “historical film project” in Arles in Provence, France. “The beauty of his films, his generosity, his joy, his poetry, and his love of music will remain with us forever.”
The statement, from his wife, children and grandchildren wished him “ Latcho Drom ”, a Roma phrase meaning “safe journey”.

Latcho Drom is also the title of Gatlif’s breakthrough 1993 film, a celebration of Roma music that moves from India to Spain, and which won the Un Certain Regard award at the Cannes film festival that year.

Gatlif had more success in 1997 with Gadjo Dilo, which featured Romain Duris as a Frenchman who is searching for a Roma singer in Romania; it won a Silver Leopard at the Locarno film festival and a César award for best original music.

articles.title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Allegedly Visited Pedophilia Chatroom, Leading to Suspension
articles.summary: More details regarding the suspension of “Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton are emerging: According to TMZ, the website has received photos from an American Airlines passenger who says they saw Thornton’s laptop opened on a “disturbing chat room” that appeared to be “images and texts that…
body: The alleged incident that led to the suspension apparently took place on an American Airlines flight in May. The passenger told TMZ that they informed a flight attendant about the chat room usage, and that authorities questioned Thornton at LAX when his flight landed. He was then given permission to leave, the website said.

Thornton’s lawyer, Allison Hart, has so far not returned requests for comment. But TMZ said she told the outlet that it was a misunderstanding, and that Thornton had “become active in suicide-prevention advocacy since losing a close family member to suicide two years ago and he has spent time visiting chat rooms offering support to individuals suffering from suicidal ideation.”

The site, she said, is “not unlawful, there is no unlawful child pornography or other pedophilic content and my client never viewed, downloaded or consumed any child pornography whether on that commercial flight in May or at any other time. In short, my client did nothing wrong.”

articles.title: Queer Edward II review – funny, touching time capsule of Derek Jarman at work
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Filmed during the making of his queer royal feature, while the director was living with HIV, the candid footage includes uproarious scenes at a Cliff Richard rehearsal.
body: There could hardly be a more vivid time-capsule film about the publicly funded British arts scene in the early 1990s than this engrossing fly-on-the-wall documentary about Derek Jarman and his movie Edward II. Based on the play by Christopher Marlowe, it is about the 14th-century English king and his love affair with his court favourite, Piers Gaveston, with Steven Waddington and Andrew Tiernan as the leads and Tilda Swinton as Queen Isabella.

The “outing” debate now in fact looks very dated and this is the one moment where you can sense that Jarman thinks that the OutRage! protesters got it wrong by harassing and bullying Cliff Richard; we see him assuring his own team later that Tatchell gave them a real telling off for this. (Did Tatchell actually do anything of the kind? Or is that what Jarman felt ought to have happened?) It’s an absorbing and affecting portrait of a dedicated artist at work.
points: Venice film festival: Filmed during the making of his queer royal feature, while the director was living with HIV, the candid footage includes uproarious scenes at a Cliff Richard rehearsal.

articles.title: Mellody Hobson Tears Up Talking About Why Husband George Lucas Was Unwilling to Compromise on Lucas Museum of Narrative Art: ‘I Saw Genius Work’
articles.summary: Mellody Hobson delivered emotional remarks about her husband George Lucas as the two hosted a “friends and family” preview on Thursday night at the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles.
body: The museum, which features 1,200 pieces from Lucas’s private collection, has been in the works for about 20 years. Located in Exposition Park and designed by Ma Yansong of MAD Architects, the museum includes 30 galleries and two restaurants.

“I thought I was tough. I thought I was strong, I thought I had a will, and then I saw George, and I was like, ‘Oh, that’s why you could only do six of those movies,’” Hobson said. “Any more would have killed you.”

“Thank you so much for being patient with us, the town, the community, everyone, as we were trying to get this all done,” Hobson said. “We are amazed that we’re limping to the finish line and the joy that we get out of this is seeing how people react to it, especially children.”

“This has been a very challenging, amazing, emotional, unexpected journey that someone from Chicago who grew up the way I did never expected to have in her whole life and say, ‘Come to my museum,’” she said. “Those words don’t even make sense for me.”

articles.title: Dolly Parton Gets New Hollywood Walk of Fame Star After Original Was Vandalized Following Her Death
articles.summary: Dolly Parton‘s star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame has been replaced after the original one was vandalized following the country superstar’s death. Parton died of cancer on Aug. 25 at age 80.
body: The outpouring of support for Parton has been immense. Earlier this week, her estate announced the first large public programs honoring the life and music of the late superstar, with events titled “DollyFest: The Celebration of a Lifetime” set to take place in Nashville and London on successive weekends in 2027.
Later this year, Dolly Parton’s “ Dolly: A True Original Musical ” is set to open on Broadway “as was Dolly’s wish.”

In a statement to Variety, the producers confirmed, “As was Dolly’s wish, the Broadway production of ‘Dolly: A True Original Musical’ will begin previews Dec. 7 at the St. James Theatre in New York City with opening set for Jan. 19, 2027, what would have been her 81 st birthday.”
Her music has also seen significant surges on Spotify. Following her death, total streams increased over 1,260% globally and 2,320% in the United States compared to the prior seven-day daily average.

articles.title: Gavin and Stacey star Rob Brydon's regret at turning down Dolly Parton interview
articles.summary: The comedian visited Dollywood in his BBC series Rob Brydon's Honky Tonk road trip.
body: Gavin and Stacey star Rob Brydon says he "regrets" turning down the chance to interview Dolly Parton after choosing to stay on a family holiday.
Brydon fronted the BBC documentary series Honky Tonk Road Trip, where he travelled across the American South to celebrate 100 years of country music.
In it he visited Dollywood, a theme park created by Parton, where Dolly's relatives had traced the lineage of the Parton and Owens sides to Wales.

He was told he could interview Parton if he returned after filming had ended, but chose to stay on his family holiday in Arizona - an opportunity he now wished he had taken because he never got to meet her before she died.

articles.title: ‘Barbara Forever’ Review: Queer Experimental Filmmaker Barbara Hammer Gets a Tactile, True and Treasurable Career Overview
articles.summary: Director Brydie O’Connor stitches together a huge mass of material in this documentary that counts Kristen Stewart among its executive producers.
body: The filmmaker Barbara Hammer, a true pathfinder in the realm of queer aesthetics, experimental filmmaking and so much more, died in 2019 at the age of 79, having made dozens of films. Judging by the footage seen in documentary Barbara Forever of her life partner and executor Florrie Burke sifting through endless boxes and film cans, it would seem Hammer was perhaps also, understandably, one of those people who find it hard to throw anything out.

But while Hammer features in nearly every frame, and most of the footage was shot or directed by the late filmmaker, viewers are also subtly aware of the guiding hand of Barbara Forever ‘s director, archival producer Brydie O’Connor. The latter also made a precursor short about Hammer, Love, Barbara (2022), and here once again she is palpable as an offscreen but collaborative editorial presence that is shaping Hammer’s material for easier consumption. That collectivist spirit is apt given that Hammer sought out younger artists, such as trans-masc filmmaker Joey Carducci, to finish as they saw fit projects that Hammer originally started.

articles.title: Fan Bingbing Sparks Carnal Desire in Invalid Father-in-Law in Wayne Wang’s ‘Diary of a Mad Old Man’ (Exclusive Toronto Clip)
articles.summary: The Asian-American director's erotically-charged drama also stars Lily Franky and will have a gala world premiere at the Toronto Film Festival.
body: With Wang’s usual artful approach to erotic desire, a perspiring Susu then tells her father-in-law she will take a shower and will leave the door open — which Utsugi judges to be a possible plea for sex.

“Why did Susu say, ‘I’ll leave the door open’?” Was it an invitation? Or maybe a tease,” Utsugi writes in his private journal. He may be a “hideous” old man, Utsugi continues to write, but he can still attract beautiful women like his daughter-in-law without raising suspicions about erotic obsessions.

Never mind Susu may well have left the shower door open should Utsugi fall and call out for help. Wayne has cracked open his own narrative door for charged encounters between Utsugi and Susu to escalate, for the boundaries between seduction and projection, intimacy and manipulation to fall away, and Diary of a Mad Old Man to be a darkly comic take on loneliness, perversity and the search for deep human connection.
